column1: # Known Layer-3 failures: comparisons that breach the blocking threshold because
# of a filed, open defect in ltl — not because the harness is miscalibrated.
# An entry suppresses the block for exactly one (scenario, file_kind, column,
# key_class) combination and is reported as XFAIL, with its issue, on every run.
# It is NOT a tolerance: the comparison still happens and the deviation is still
# printed.
# Entries are self-clearing. If a registered comparison PASSES, the engine fails
# the run with "known failure no longer reproduces" — so the fix cannot land
# without the entry being removed in the same change.
# Columns:
#   scenario    — scenario id from scenarios.tsv
#   file_kind   — messages | stats
#   column      — the CSV column whose comparison is expected to breach
#   key_class   — merged (row key contains the consolidation wildcard '*')
#                 | any
#   issue       — the open defect this is waiting on
#   note        — why, in one line
# #469: consolidated rows are addressed on each cluster's own bin edges, so the
# members must be projected onto a shared geometry before they can be combined.
# A consolidated row's percentiles are derived from the member histograms of the
# keys the row absorbed, projected onto one shared geometry. The oracle derives
# the same row by pooling those keys' raw durations into a single histogram. One
# projection is not zero projections, so the two cannot agree closer than one
# bucket - 4.44% at the per-message surface's default 53 buckets per decade.
# Every entry below is inside that bound; IQR entries are larger because an IQR
# is a difference of two percentiles and carries both.
# Attribution history, because it has moved twice and the reasoning is the point.
# Registered against #459 (combination order) on 2026-08-26, on the assumption
# that its compounding was the cause. It was not: #459 landed on 2026-08-27,
# removing the compounding and proving order-independence, and these comparisons
# still breach. They moved to #460 (percentile source) with the bound as the
# stated cause. They are not #460's either: #460 removes the display projection
# that precedes histogram and heatmap percentiles, and the merged rows below do
# not take that path - their percentiles already come from the un-projected
# streaming entry, and their one projection is the collapse onto the shared
# geometry. Measured on real grouped rows, that single projection leaves the
# one-bucket bound on 1.54% (tomcat) and 2.08% (thingworx) of evaluations; see
# features/459-bin-counter-combination-order.md sections 7 and 9.
# They clear under #469, which addresses consolidated rows on a shared bucket
# grid and so performs no projection at all. Until then they are the accepted
# residual bound, documented as such in features/187-histogram-bin-counter-
# percentiles.md section R4. The entries are self-clearing and the engine will
# insist.
